question: Should OpenClaw allow sandboxed sessions to request ACP host or worker spawns, and which security boundary should own that capability?
rationale: The implementation could take several shapes, but automation should not choose whether sandboxed sessions may cross into host-side ACP execution or whether ACP must move into isolated workers.

options.title: Prefer Isolated ACP Workers
options.body: Extend the execution-backend/profile design so ACP runs in a sandboxed worker or sidecar with explicit auth, workspace, secret, and lifecycle boundaries before enabling sandboxed requesters.

options.title: Approve Audited Host Bridge
options.body: Add an opt-in host-side ACP proxy with narrow spawn, steer, and cancel APIs, allowlisting, rate limits, and durable audit logs for operators who accept controlled privilege escalation.

options.title: Keep Current Block
options.body: Continue documenting that sandboxed sessions should use `runtime="subagent"` or run ACP-capable harnesses inside the container until a stronger security design is sponsored.

recommendation.title: Prefer Isolated ACP Workers
recommendation.body: Extend the execution-backend/profile design so ACP runs in a sandboxed worker or sidecar with explicit auth, workspace, secret, and lifecycle boundaries before enabling sandboxed requesters.

likelyOwner.reason: osolmaz merged the current ACP sandbox hardening and is the best available owner signal for deciding whether that boundary should change.
